transcript.answer:
ADR-002 (accepted 2026-09-25) settled this when it rejected PR #261 review comment 4098626654, which proposed dropping the card and letting the model phrase the answer in free text. The ADR gives these reasons for always rendering a deterministic card:
1. Hallucination and compliance risk. The EU AI Act data-flow record and the docs/danish-review.md rows promise that the customer reads delivery status verbatim from the TMS. A paraphrased delivery time or ETA is the one hallucination the pilot can't afford.
2. The card-rate KPI needs cards. SC-006 sets a card rate of at least 90% by 2026-Q4. A prose answer gives no measurable denominator, so the KPI can only be measured if the answer is always a card.
3. The thumbs-up KPI needs cards. SC-007 sets a thumbs-up rate of at least 80% by 2026-Q4. Ratings attach to card turns, and a prose answer produces no rating.
4. The not-found case is also a deterministic card, because the model can't invent a shipment it didn't fetch.
5. The assistant's own text stays suppressed. FR-043 of the support-agent-tms-tools spec is being amended to allow a deterministic-render tool.

The reviewer's worry was that a rigid card reduces the model's flexibility. The ADR judged that cost smaller than the risks above.

judgements.reason: The answer covers the card-rate KPI SC-006 (≥90% by 2026-Q4) needing card turns as the denominator, the verbatim TMS compliance promise with paraphrased ETA as the unaffordable hallucination, and the rejection of the PR #261 free-text proposal on 2026-09-25; its extra details do not contradict the gold answer.
